text: {"features":[{"evidence":"\"Go as my daily driver\"","name":"Go centrality","description":"This dimension captures how clearly the letter establishes Go as a primary production language for the applicant's backend work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not establish meaningful Go use, or only lists Go among many languages without context."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Go experience but not as a main language, or gives little evidence of production use."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that Go is a primary or daily language in production systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows Go as a primary language and ties it to relevant backend ownership such as services, infrastructure, or guardrail systems."}]},{"evidence":"\"Python became my workhorse\"","name":"Python fluency","description":"This dimension captures the depth and production relevance of the applicant's Python experience.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no clear Python evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python in passing or as incidental scripting experience."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, services, or prototypes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Portrays Python as a production-grade workhorse with concrete examples such as typed services, internal tools, data pipelines, automation layers, or AI agent components."}]},{"evidence":"\"automates triage of incoming vulnerability reports\"","name":"Vulnerability triage automation","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter shows direct experience building systems that intake, classify, route, or otherwise automate vulnerability handling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no clear example of vulnerability-handling automation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation generally but not a concrete triage workflow."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes building triage tooling such as classification, routing, deduplication, or queue automation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows end-to-end triage automation with concrete mechanism or impact, such as reduced manual work, returned expert hours, or a queue that became largely self-serve."}]},{"evidence":"\"performed security assessments\"","name":"Security assessment depth","description":"This dimension captures how much real assessment practice the letter conveys, from vague review language to concrete security evaluation methods.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no security assessment evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions reviews or assessments in broad terms without saying what was done."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface mapping, or fix validation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents repeated or hands-on assessment practice with a clear method or mindset, such as builder's-eye review, attacker perspective, or formal remediation follow-through."}]},{"evidence":"\"Python agents ... Go services constrain\"","name":"Agentic tooling architecture","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter shows real design ownership of agent-based systems rather than only mentioning AI or automation generically.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no clear agent-based system example."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents or automation without explaining the architecture."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a Go-plus-Python agent system with distinct roles for agents and services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains deliberate agent boundaries, permissions, auditing, autonomy, or guardrails in a way that demonstrates architectural ownership."}]},{"evidence":"\"LLM-based features that had to behave predictably\"","name":"Applied AI deployment maturity","description":"This dimension captures how production-ready the applicant's AI experience sounds, especially around reliability and operational discipline.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no AI experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI or language models vaguely or as exploratory exposure."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes shipping AI-backed or LLM-backed features in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows mature production AI practice by discussing evaluation, reliability, safeguards, or failure modes around deployed models."}]},{"evidence":"\"redesigning an in-memory index\"","name":"Data structure reasoning","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter gives evidence of algorithmic judgment beyond simply claiming strength in data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no algorithmic evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims algorithmic strength without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives one concrete redesign or optimization driven by a better data structure or algorithm choice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong algorithmic judgment tied to system tractability, performance, or correctness, often through multiple concrete examples or a high-impact one."}]},{"evidence":"\"the logical next step\"","name":"Role-specific motivation","description":"This dimension captures how convincingly the letter explains why this exact job fits the applicant's trajectory rather than expressing generic interest.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows generic interest in a software role or in security without explaining why this job specifically."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"States interest in the role but mostly in broad company or job terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Connects prior experience to the specific mandate of this role."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Makes a compelling case that this exact role is the natural next step in the applicant's development and goals."}]},{"evidence":"\"improvements there are inherited by every team downstream\"","name":"Foundational platform orientation","description":"This dimension captures whether the applicant values central infrastructure work for its broad downstream leverage.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows no clear interest in foundational or shared systems."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses general interest in infrastructure without a leverage argument."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly values central or foundational teams because improvements propagate across many users or teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Repeatedly frames impact in terms of downstream leverage, inherited improvements, or company-wide capacity enabled by platform work."}]},{"evidence":"\"make the secure path the easy path\"","name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter frames security work as helping developers succeed rather than only as enforcement or review.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no indication of serving developer users."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions secure defaults or reduced toil only abstractly."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly frames security as helping developers do the right thing more easily."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently emphasizes low-friction developer enablement, such as proactive assistance, avoiding policing, or embedding secure behavior in defaults and tooling."}]},{"evidence":"\"too many signals, too few experts\"","name":"Security automation framing","description":"This dimension captures whether the applicant treats security operations as a scaling problem that can be improved through systems design.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Treats security work mainly as isolated tasks or incidents."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions automation as useful but without a clear scaling argument."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Frames vulnerability handling or response as a systems problem that can reduce manual workload at scale."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Articulates a strong scaling thesis, such as multiplying scarce expert judgment, enabling variant analysis, or turning reactive queues into capacity-building systems."}]},{"evidence":"\"reviewing external contributions and shipping releases\"","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter shows ownership in open source, ranging from small fixes to sustained maintenance responsibility.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no open-source evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional fixes or contributions."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes regular upstream patching or ongoing maintenance responsibility."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows stewardship of an actively used project or library, including reviews, releases, roadmap decisions, or support for external users."}]},{"evidence":"\"capture-the-flag competitions\"","name":"Competitive offensive practice","description":"This dimension captures whether the applicant demonstrates ongoing offensive-security practice outside ordinary job claims.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no ongoing offensive-security practice."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional CTF participation or informal adversarial practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular serious CTF participation or strong placements."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents sustained high-level competitive offensive practice as a deliberate part of skill development."}]},{"evidence":"\"OSCP certification\"","name":"Security certification","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter offers a formal security credential and how hands-on that credential appears to be.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mentions no security credential."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or another fundamentals-oriented certification."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions a hands-on credential such as OSCP or another exam explicitly demonstrating practical exploitation ability."}]},{"evidence":"\"distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics\"","name":"Personal systems building","description":"This dimension captures how much the applicant uses side projects to demonstrate self-directed systems engineering beyond their day job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no side project, or only a generic small app with little technical challenge."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small personal project that shows initiative but limited systems complexity."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a substantive self-directed build with meaningful backend or infrastructure complexity."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Uses a personal project to demonstrate ambitious systems thinking, such as replication, failover, consensus, exactly-once delivery, or similarly hard failure cases."}]},{"evidence":"\"7 years ... launched 6 production services\"","name":"Professional backend tenure","description":"This dimension captures the amount and scope of hands-on production software experience the letter claims.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Experience level is unclear or appears below the role's minimum expectations."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Meets the minimum with limited scope, such as a few years and a small number of launched services."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows solid professional scope, typically multiple years with several production services tested, maintained, or launched."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows especially broad scope, such as long tenure plus repeated launches or ownership across many production services."}]},{"evidence":"\"Bachelor's degree ... Master's degree ... Doctoral degree\"","name":"Academic attainment","description":"This dimension captures the highest formal educational credential presented in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not state a qualifying degree or equivalent preparation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"States a bachelor's degree or equivalent."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States a master's degree."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"States a doctoral degree."}]},{"evidence":"\"measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned\"","name":"Evidence specificity","description":"This dimension captures how much the letter supports claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, or outcomes instead of relying on generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on broad claims or adjectives with little supporting evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Names relevant activities but gives little mechanism, scope, or outcome."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Uses concrete examples with specific tasks, systems, or decisions."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Supplies multiple concrete examples that show mechanism, scope, and effect rather than merely asserting fit."}]},{"evidence":"\"Sofwtare\" \"seccurity\"","name":"Writing polish","description":"This dimension captures the level of spelling, grammar, and sentence-level professionalism in the letter itself.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent spelling, grammar, or phrasing problems undermine confidence or attention to detail."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Noticeable errors are present but the letter remains understandable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Writing is mostly clean and professional with only minor issues."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Writing is polished, precise, and easy to follow throughout."}]},{"evidence":"\"typed, tested services\"","name":"Reliability mindset","description":"This dimension captures whether the letter presents dependable engineering, guardrails, and failure handling as central habits rather than incidental concerns.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows little evidence of concern for correctness, failure modes, or guardrails."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses reliability or rigor as a value but with limited supporting detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives concrete signs of a reliability mindset, such as testing, boundaries, failure recovery, typed tooling, or dependable operation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Makes rigorous, dependable engineering a central theme and supports it with repeated examples across security, infrastructure, or AI work."}]},{"evidence":"\"work alongside dedicated security engineers\"","name":"Security collaboration posture","description":"This dimension captures whether the applicant presents themselves as someone who will collaborate productively with specialist security partners and internal users.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no clear indication of collaboration with security stakeholders or partner teams."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Implies coordination with security work but focuses mostly on individual contribution."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly references partnering with security engineers, reviewers, or internal users."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows a strong collaborative posture, such as eagerness to learn from specialists, close service to partner teams, or repeated framing around shared problem-solving."}]}]}
